options: Revenue minus Expenses equals Net Income
Debits equal Credits times two
Assets equal Liabilities plus Equity
Cash equals Assets minus Liabilities
questions.explain: Assets = Liabilities + Equity is the foundational equation that every accounting system must keep in balance at all times.

questions.q: In the accounting equation, what does Equity represent?
options: The owners' residual claim on the business after liabilities are subtracted from assets
The total amount of cash the business has on hand
Everything the business owes to outside parties
A tax the business must pay each year
questions.explain: Equity is what's left for the owners once everything owed to outsiders (liabilities) is subtracted from everything the business owns (assets).

questions.q: Meridian Fusion Consulting borrows $20,000 to buy a server. What happens to the accounting equation?
options: Only liabilities increase; nothing else changes
Both assets and liabilities increase by $20,000, keeping the equation balanced
Only assets increase; nothing else changes
Equity decreases by $20,000
questions.explain: The server (an asset) and the loan obligation (a liability) both increase by the same amount, so the equation stays in balance.

questions.q: What is the term for the principle that every transaction must affect the accounting equation in at least two places by equal amounts?
options: Single-entry accounting
Trial balancing
Equity dilution
Double-entry accounting
questions.explain: Double-entry accounting is the rule that every transaction has offsetting effects of equal value, keeping the equation balanced.

questions.q: Why will Oracle Fusion General Ledger reject a journal entry where total debits do not equal total credits?
options: Because Oracle limits the number of lines in a journal
Because unbalanced journals are too large for the database to store
Because it is enforcing the accounting equation, which must always stay in balance
Oracle Fusion does not actually check this
questions.explain: An unbalanced journal would break the accounting equation, so the system enforces the same rule that underlies all of accounting.
